props.title: I'll Be Home for Christmas

sections.content: **I'll Be Home for Christmas** (1998) sits firmly in Disney's late 90s teen comedy catalogue, starring Jonathan Taylor Thomas at the height of his "Home Improvement" fame. The film follows the well-worn "getting home for the holidays" formula established by classics like **Planes, Trains & Automobiles** (1987), but aims squarely at a younger audience. It's part of a specific moment in family entertainment when Disney was churning out theatrical releases starring their TV talent, similar to **Model Behavior** (2000) with Justin Timberlake and **Smart House** (1999) with Ryan Merriman.

sections.content: The "race home for Christmas" subgenre peaked in the 1980s-90s with varying degrees of success. While **I'll Be Home for Christmas** (1998) takes a lighter approach, films like **The Sure Thing** (1985) and **Dutch** (1991) used the cross-country journey premise to explore deeper themes of personal growth and family relationships. The formula typically involves an entitled protagonist who learns humility through travel mishaps, with **Jingle All the Way** (1996) offering a suburban twist on the concept. SUBHEAD: Teen Holiday Movies of the Late 90s

The late 90s saw a wave of teen-focused holiday films that mixed comedy with light romance. **Jack Frost** (1998) released the same year with a more fantastical premise, while **Snow Day** (2000) and **Richie Rich's Christmas Wish** (1998) targeted similar demographics. These films often featured TV stars making the jump to film, like **I'll Be Home for Christmas** (1998) did with JTT, establishing a template Disney would continue into the 2000s with their DCOMs (Disney Channel Original Movies).
